newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Canada's Chretien arrives on Philippine visit.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien arrives on Philippine visit.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien arrived in Manila on Tuesday on a three-day visit during which he will take over chairmanship of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
The Canadian leader, heading a 350-member strong business mission, arrived in the city from South Korea, Canadian Embassy officials said.
Philippine officials said Chretien was to meet President Fidel Ramos later in the day and attend a ceremony at which Canada would assume chairmanship of the 18-member APEC.
The Philippines headed APEC in 1996, when the trade grouping adopted an action plan on fulfilling its goal of completely freeing trade within the region.
Chretien has combined the visit to take over APEC's chairmanship along with a business mission that aims to increase trade with the Philippines.
Canadian Embassy officials said about 350 businessmen were accompanying Chretien on the Manila visit, after which he will go to Thailand.

Officials said the business delegation, called Team Canada, was expected to go home with several business deals including contracts for telecommunications equipment, software development and an air services pact.
The deals are expected to be announced at a signing ceremony on Wednesday, they said.
